newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan economic recovery becoming firmer - BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Japan economic recovery becoming firmer - BOJ.

text.p: Japan's economy is still recovering gradually and the recovery is becoming firmer, Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita told a news conference on Wednesday.

"Our view has been that the economy is continuing to recover gradually, and at the moment the strength of the recovery is becoming firmer. Reports received from BOJ branch managers back this up," Matsushita said.
The BOJ held a regular meeting of its branch managers on Monday and Tuesday.

But for the economy to securely move on to a self-sustaining recovery track, it was important for the favourable economic cycle of production leading to an increase in incomes and thus spending to strengthen further, he said.
"We still need to confirm these movements."
He added: "Our monetary policy for now, as I have said before, is to put emphasis on securing the basis for economic recovery while keeping careful watch on economic developments."

Asked about the impact of the weaker yen on Japan's economy and prices, he said the surplus in Japan's trade balance with other countries had stopped shrinking since the correction of the strong yen last year. This had also helped to push up corporate profits.
"Prices of imports have risen with the move in the yen's exchange rate, but supply/demand conditions here are rather loose. So it has yet to push up overall domestic prices."

Matsushita said companies had not dropped their cautious stance towards economic prospects. This was due to remaining pressures from structural adjustments, a decrease in support for the economy from fiscal measures and the plunge in Tokyo stock prices.

"Companies cannot put aside their uncertainties about future prospects when looking at these factors," Matsushita said. On various factors supporting the BOJ's views on the economy, he said public spending had already declined while housing investment was still at high levels. Net exports had stopped declining and private consumption was gradually rising.
He said corporate capital investment was steadily rising, and this trend was spreading to smaller firms despite the pressures of changes in industrial structure.
Matsushita said one reason for this was that companies of all sizes were actively developing new products and entering new businesses.
The pace of increase in production was speeding up and some improvement could be seen in employment conditions, such as some companies increasing their hiring of new graduates.

Matsushita said it was important for the central bank's independence and the transparency of its decision-making to be strengthened in the revision of the BOJ law now being considered by a government committee.

Asked whether Japan needed to boost funds to be used to cope with future bank failures, Matsushita said he did not think the current situation called for authorities to think of securing further funds for that purpose.

He said Japan's "Big Bang" financial reforms would introduce more competition and create more business opportunities. There there might be business failures in the process, but that should not undermine the overall financial system.
He added that measures taken so far by the government to cope with possible failures of financial institutions were sufficient.
